g.title: G
Receive verified block data. Meaning: The validator checks signatures and Merkle proofs before it stores new shreds. Purpose: These checks connect the received data to the expected block and leader.

Block data available. Meaning: The validator has the complete block and gets missing ancestor data as necessary. Purpose: Execution needs both the block’s transactions and the state from its parent chain.

R01: All block data present. When: The validator has enough valid data to reconstruct the complete block. Action: Make B available for execution. Reason: The validator cannot execute or check a complete block from insufficient data.

a.xlink:title: The validator cannot execute or check a complete block from insufficient data.
R01: All block data present

g.title: Execute the block. Meaning: Agave replays the block and its parents. A frozen bank records completed local execution. Purpose: The validator needs this execution result for ordinary voting and local root advancement.
g.text: Agave: execute B and its parents
Bank is frozen; block ID is known

g.title: R02: Execute the block. When: B and the required parent data are available. Action: Execute the parent chain and B. Reason: The transactions need the parent’s state to produce the correct next state.

a.xlink:title: The transactions need the parent's state to produce the correct next state.
R02: Execute the block

g.title: Completed-block event. Meaning: Agave sends Block(B) to the voting loop after replay completes. Purpose: The loop can check initial voting and whether stored finality proofs now have usable local state.

R03: Replay complete. When: Agave completes replay and has the block ID. Action: Send Block(B) to the voting loop. Reason: The current implementation checks execution before its normal initial notar vote.

a.xlink:title: The current implementation checks execution before its normal initial notar vote.
R03: Replay complete

g.title: Execution hash mismatch. Meaning: The exact final block is present, but the validator computes an execution hash different from the expected hash. Purpose: Agave stops and saves diagnostics because its local execution state disagrees with the final block’s expected state.

R13: Final execution hash differs. When: The bank is frozen and its block ID matches a final block, but its expected execution hash differs. Action: Stop the validator and save diagnostics. Reason: The validator computed a different state for the block that the network finalized. It cannot safely continue from that state.

a.xlink:title: The validator computed a different state for the block that the network finalized. It cannot safely continue from that state.
R13: Final execution hash\ndiffers

g.title: Check the local root requirements. Meaning: The block must be above the root. Its frozen bank and block ID must match, and local first-vote history must exist. Purpose: These are local readiness checks. They do not add another network quorum or require this validator’s own FinalVote.
g.text: AND the bank is present and frozen
AND its block ID matches the proof
AND a local first vote exists?

g.title: R10: New replay result. When: A completed-block event arrives while final decisions are stored. Action: Check whether any final block can now become the local root. Reason: Replay can supply the last missing local requirement after the certificate arrived.

a.xlink:title: Replay can supply the last missing local requirement after the certificate arrived.
R10: New replay result

g.title: Evidence requires block data. Meaning: A certificate or a fallback parent check identifies a block whose data the validator needs. Purpose: A vote proof does not contain all block transactions or ancestor data.

Repair missing data. Meaning: The validator requests the block by hash and checks the returned slice and shred data. Purpose: The hash distinguishes different blocks in the same slot. Missing or invalid responses require more requests.
g.text: Get the missing block by hash
Check each response; retry if necessary

g.title: R04: Required data missing. When: A certificate or the fallback parent check requires block data that the validator lacks. Action: Request that specific block. Reason: The certificate does not contain all transactions or the complete parent data.

a.xlink:title: The certificate does not contain all transactions or the complete parent data.
R04: Required data missing

g.title: R06: Repair complete. When: Verified responses supply the required block data. Action: Make the block available for execution. Reason: The validator now has the data identified by the block hash.

a.xlink:title: The validator now has the data identified by the block hash.
R06: Repair complete

g.title: R05: Response absent or invalid. When: A repair request does not supply valid missing data. Action: Try another request to a sampled peer. Reason: A faulty or unavailable peer must not find the repaired block’s contents.

a.xlink:title: A faulty or unavailable peer must not find the repaired block's contents.
R05: Response absent or\ninvalid

g.title: Finality proof verified. Meaning: The validator has a valid fast certificate or the ordinary notar and final certificate pair for B. Purpose: This establishes the consensus result even if the block data or local execution is still missing.

Remember the final decision. Meaning: The validator keeps B as a final block while it repairs data and checks local root conditions. Purpose: Incomplete local execution must not erase a final decision established by certificates.

R07: Final proof accepted. When: The validator verifies a fast-final certificate or the required pair of certificates. Action: Remember B as final. Request repair and check the local root conditions. Reason: The validator must preserve the final decision even if local execution is not yet complete.

a.xlink:title: The validator must preserve the final decision even if local execution is not yet complete.
R07: Final proof accepted

g.title: R08: Final block data missing. When: The final block or its required ancestors are missing. Action: Request the missing data. Reason: The validator needs that data before it can get the final block’s local state.

a.xlink:title: The validator needs that data before it can get the final block's local state.
R08: Final block data\nmissing

g.title: R09: Check local conditions. When: The validator has a stored final decision for B. Action: Check the bank, block ID, vote history, and current root. Reason: A valid finality proof alone does not establish that local execution is ready.

a.xlink:title: A valid finality proof alone does not establish that local execution is ready.
R09: Check local conditions

g.title: R11: A condition is false. When: At least one local root condition is false. Action: Keep the final decision and wait for the missing requirement. Reason: The validator must not advance its local root to data or state it cannot yet use.

a.xlink:title: The validator must not advance its local root to data or state it cannot yet use.
R11: A condition is false

g.title: Advance the local root. Meaning: Agave selects the highest eligible final block and uses its executed state as the fixed local chain base. Purpose: It can then remove obsolete local state and update commitment information.
g.text: Select the highest eligible final block

g.title: R12: All conditions are true. When: A final block above the root meets every local requirement. Action: Select the highest eligible final block. Advance the root and remove unnecessary state. Reason: The validator can now use the final chain as its local execution base.

a.xlink:title: The validator can now use the final chain as its local execution base.
R12: All conditions are\ntrue
